title: Model catalog demo - SageClinic
next_steps: Ethan to send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and model cost examples
Maya to share compatibility matrix and benchmark spreadsheet
action_items: Ethan Park - Send pricing and committed capacity options - 2026-12-17
Maya Chen - Share model compatibility matrix and benchmark CSV - 2026-12-16
Priya Nair - Provide sample prompt set and top-10 latency SLOs - 2026-12-18
summary: Redwood walked SageClinic through the Model Catalog in Console and Optimize recommendations. Focus on choosing open models for clinical summarization, benchmarking results for latency/cost tradeoffs, and compatibility with private deployments (VPC/KMS). Customer leaned toward hosted pilot but wants dedicated capacity or VPC for PHI after pilot; requested security docs and benchmark spreadsheets.
topics: Next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, im Ethan AE on the account, with Maya our SE and Liam from product.
[00:10] Dr. Lopez: Morning, thanks. I'm Maria, CTO at SageClinic, Priya's on from ML, Jared from infra.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): we'll demo the Model Catalog, show how you pick open models, the benchmarks tab, and the compatibility matrix in the console. we'll also run through Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.
[00:35] Priya (SageClinic): high level we want to do clinical note summarization and triage routing; cost is a big factor, latency needs to be under 300ms p95 on short inputs if possible.
[00:50] Maya: got it. in the catalog we surface curated open models - Llama-3-70B, Mistral-Instruct, and a few optimized variants (like llama-3-70b-8bit and mistral-7b-quant). each listing shows throughput, tokens/s, and a benchmark panel.
[01:10] Jared: when you say 8-bit and quant variants, are those fully supported across our Dedicated GPU options? we run A100s and a mix of T4s.
[01:25] Maya: yes, compatibility matrix maps model variants to hardware. e.g. 8-bit llama-3-70b runs on A100 with tensor cores and gives best latency; 4-bit quant variants are recommended on T4 and cheaper GPUs but may see slight quality diffs. note: some perf numbers are from our internal bench - real results vary by prompt distribution.
[01:50] Ethan: quick note on hosted vs dedicated: hosted is easiest to start, cheap pilot, but for PHI you'll likely want Private (VPC) or Dedicated with encryption-in-transit and KMS integration.
[02:05] Dr. Lopez: we will need SOC 2 and KMS for any PHI, and logs for audits. can you point to those?
[02:15] Ethan: absolutely; i'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs after. we also have RBAC & SSO (SAML).
[02:25] Maya: back to the catalog, here's the benchmark tab - you can filter by seq length, batch size, and region. we show p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and a cost per 1k tokens estimate. for your workload (short notes, ~200 tokens) the 7b quant models sometimes hit 120ms p95 on A100 but cost less.
[02:50] Priya: what about semantic quality? we care about hallucinations and factuality, not just latency.
[03:00] Maya: we include model eval snippets and community-run evals; Optimize can run your prompt set and produce ROUGE/BLEU-like scores or custom metrics. for clinical summarization we recommend testing with a 100-prompt eval to measure regression.
[03:20] Jared: the compatibility matrix - can we export that CSV? we want it in our internal procurement docs.
[03:28] Maya: yes, there's an export button. i'll share the file as well.
[03:35] Ethan: some customers run a staged approach: start Hosted with open-model pilot, then move to Dedicated reservation for throughput, then to Private VPC for PHI. keeps time-to-value quick.
[03:50] Dr. Lopez: regarding costs, can you show example numbers for Llama-3-70b-8bit vs Mistral-7b-quant on A100?
[04:02] Maya: in the benchmark panel here's a sample: 70b-8bit on A100 - p95 180ms, cost est $0.75 per 1k tokens; mistral-7b-quant p95 95ms, cost est $0.22 per 1k tokens. those are ballpark - Optimize can run a batch to give exact numbers for your prompt set.
[04:30] Priya: 180ms p95 for 70b is ok but the cost is higher; we'd likely start with 7b quant to validate quality.
[04:40] Maya: that's a common tradeoff. also the catalog shows recommended quant profiles per model, e.g. 4-bit q4 or 8-bit q8 and notes on quality delta.
[04:55] Ethan: i also want to flag autoscaling/burst behavior for Dedicated - you can reserve baseline throughput and allow burst to hosted pool if needed. good for spiky triage traffic.
[05:10] Jared: in Private deployment, do you manage the control plane or is it customer-managed? network-wise how does VPC peering work?
[05:20] Liam (Redwood Product): Private has a customer-managed control plane and optional managed deployer. VPC peering uses standard cloud peering with routes you control; we support customer KMS or HSM for key management.
[05:40] Dr. Lopez: any examples of customers in health that did this?
[05:46] Ethan: we have a couple anonymized case studies; i'll link them.
[05:52] Priya: can Optimize suggest batching sizes that meet our 300ms p95 target while minimizing cost?
[06:00] Maya: yes, Optimize runs a policy search - takes your SLOs and will recommend batch size, kv cache usage, and whether to use prefix caching for repeated prompts. it also suggests model-quant combos.
[06:15] Dr. Lopez: about KV cache - does Redwood do prefix caching across requests for same patient sessions? we want reduced cost for repeated short interactions.
[06:26] Maya: yes, prefix/KV cache is supported; the console shows estimated cost reduction if enabled. slight caveat: for PHI you need to ensure cache retention policies meet your compliance.
[06:40] Jared: anything special for auditor logs? long term retention?
[06:45] Ethan: we offer long retention as an add-on and logs integrate with customer SIEM via S3/Cloudwatch exports and support for log redaction.
[06:58] Priya: back to model quality - if we pick 7b quant and see regression, what's the rollback path?
[07:06] Maya: the catalog lets you pin versions and do canary rollouts; you can auto-fallback to a higher-quality variant if latency or quality thresholds fail.
[07:20] Dr. Lopez: ok let's walk through a quick demo of choosing a model and running an eval.
[07:28] Maya: sure - opening the console now. (screen share audio) you can see the catalog search, we filter by "instruction-tuned" and "open-source"; here's the Llama-3-70b entry but note we also have curated smaller variants.
[07:48] [screen noise]
[07:55] Maya: clicking Benchmarks, selecting seq len 200, batch 1, region us-east-1. these numbers are from our perf lab and from customer runs.
[08:10] Priya: that benchmark table - is the p95 computed on synthetic workload or real traces?
[08:16] Maya: synthetic with a mix of real traces. we also have an option to upload your traces to get tailored numbers.
[08:25] Priya: we'll upload a sample of 500 notes once you share the steps.
[08:30] Maya: perfect. also note the compatibility matrix here - columns for A100, T4, and CPU-only. green means supported with recommended quant profile.
[08:42] Jared: I see some yellow cells. what do those mean?
[08:45] Maya: yellow means supported but expect lower perf or only via our 8-bit path; red means unsupported.
[08:52] Ethan: quick interjection, some names in the console are abbreviated - transcriber sometimes shows Speaker 1 for Maya.
[08:58] Dr. Lopez: ha, that's fine.
[09:02] Maya: now switching to Optimize - here's a run for a sample prompt set we ran internally. the output shows recommended batch size 4, kv cache enabled, and quant profile q4_0 for a 7b model. estimated cost drop 60% with 10% latency increase.
[09:25] Priya: can we tune the objective to penalize latency stronger? we're ok with modest cost increase to keep p95 < 300ms.
[09:30] Maya: yes you can set SLOs and weight latency vs cost; Optimize will return Pareto frontier options.
[09:38] Jared: for the pilot, how long to get representative benchmarks?
[09:42] Ethan: typically 1-2 weeks to run a 1k-5k prompt eval and capacity tests; if you provide prompt set and sample traffic we can do faster.
[09:55] Dr. Lopez: ok, timeline: we'd like a hosted pilot next week, then decision for Dedicated/VPC by quarter end.
[10:02] Ethan: noted. we'll follow up with docs and a kickoff invite.
[10:08] Maya: one last callout on the compatibility matrix - it includes recommended CUDA and driver versions, and notes on performance flags we use in the kernel selection.
[10:22] Priya: any special network requirements for low jitter?
[10:27] Liam: we recommend colocated region and minimal NAT hops; for Private dedicated deployments we can help architect for low jitter.
[10:36] [slight crosstalk]
[10:40] Priya: ok, maybe a quick question - we use internal tokenization slightly different, does Redwood accept tokenized inputs or only raw text?
[10:48] Maya: both; API accepts raw text and you can also send pre-tokenized arrays for exact token accounting.
[10:55] Dr. Lopez: will you provide a sample pipeline for ingesting notes, anonymizing, and sending to the pilot?
[11:02] Ethan: yes, we'll include a best-practices doc; we'll also include instructions for redaction and minimal necessary retention.
[11:10] Priya: any limitations on model variants for private/offline air-gapped installs?
[11:16] Maya: some heavy-weight optimized kernels require proprietary drivers; in air-gapped installs we include flexible builds but latency may differ. we'll surface that in the compatibility CSV.
[11:30] Jared: curious on fallback policies - if primary model hits an error, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[11:36] Maya: yes, rollout policies support failover to pinned compatible variant; config via console.
[11:44] Dr. Lopez: ok, this is helpful. let's capture next steps.
[11:49] Ethan: recap: Ethan send pricing and SOC2/security docs, Maya shares compatibility matrix, Priya to send prompt set, schedule pilot kickoff.
[11:58] Priya: we'll aim to share prompts by Friday.
[12:03] Ethan: great, i'll send the follow-up with links. thanks everyone.
[12:10] [call ends]
notes: Transcript contains typical speech artifacts: some speaker labels generic, occasional mis-transcriptions (KV cash, quanta). references to shared artifacts: compatibility-matrix.csv, benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx, security-pack.pdf (links to be sent).
